neighbours.label: The baseline of a superlative record claim: the token naming when record-keeping or memory starts ('since records began', 'since record keeping', 'in recorded history', 'as long as I can remember'), vs 'records' or 'since' outside a superlative baseline
fire: Last July was the hottest month in Spain since records began in 1880.
Analysts said the drought was the worst since record keeping started in the region.
The flood reached its highest level in recorded history last spring.
Sales fell to the lowest point since official records began.
Our town has held the parade for as long as anyone can remember.
The lake froze earlier than at any time since records were first kept.
Snowfall this winter was the heaviest in recorded history for the valley.
Officials called it the deadliest season since records began a century ago.
quiet: Last July the archive in Spain digitized its records from 1880.
Analysts said the farm kept careful records of rainfall each week.
The flood damaged the town hall and several shops last spring.
Sales staff updated the customer records every Friday afternoon.
Our town held the parade on Sunday and everyone came out.
The lake froze in early December, and children skated on it.
Snowfall this winter closed the mountain road for three days.
Officials moved the old records into a new building downtown.

predictions: Baseline items reach 0.5-0.85; 'records' in other uses and non-superlative 'since' stay under 0.1.
notes: Card: top peaks ' records' in 'smallest extent since records began' (-70.5), ' can' in 'as long as I can remember', ' recorded' in 'lowest level in recorded history', ' back' in 'data that go back to 1979'. Probe: 'since records began' 0.837, 'since record keeping' 0.813, 'as long as he can remember' 0.585, 'recorded history' 0.519; but 'wettest month since the new mayor' leaked 0.444 on ' since', so near misses avoid superlative + since; 'records were kept in a box' 0.030, 'since he was a small child' 0.073.
